messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx from hosted-api in us-west-2c (AZc). Multiple customers reporting failed model calls, partial traffic loss. Auto-scaling and healthchecks show elevated LB 504s.

maria (oncall): I'm on it, picking up the page. Anyone from networking awake? @oliver?

oliver (net): awake, looking. seeing a spike in route table modification events around 2026-02-18T02:03Z for rt-0a1b2c3d (AZc private). Could be propagation issue. Pulling route table and NAT status.

maria (oncall): current customer impact? Support dashboards said ~30% of production requests failing for a subset of hosts in us-west-2c.

sophie (support): Confirmed — several enterprise customers on Dedicated capacity hitting 504/502 errors. We're triaging support tickets and telling customers we're investigating. No PII exposed.

oliver (net): quick AWS check:
```
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids rt-0a1b2c3d --region us-west-2
```
Output shows default route to igw detached for some associations; several subnet associations show a different route-table (rt-0f9e8d7c) after recent infra deploy. Looks like a route-table swap for AZc private subnets without updating NAT affinity.

kevin (sre): So packets from private subnets in AZc are being routed to a route table without nat-gateway/egress path -> egress blackhole. That explains 5xx from downstream model endpoints. Any recent terraform PRs?

maria (oncall): @deploy-bot which change deployed near 02:00Z

deploy-bot: Deploy #2026.2.318 applied at 2026-02-18T02:01Z by infra-cibot, included network/route-tables update PR #432 - swapped route-table associations to enable new transit config.

oliver (net): PR #432 changed association for subnets in AZc to rt-0f9e8d7c. That RT is missing the 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-xxxxxxxx mapping for the private subnet range. It looks like a merge-time drift: rt-0f9e8d7c belongs to a different AZ pair and doesn't have NAT mapping.

maria (oncall): We need mitigation plan. Do we revert association change or add routes to the RT? Which is fastest and safest?

oliver (net): Fastest: re-associate affected subnets back to rt-0a1b2c3d (the previous route table with nat). Alternative: add 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-xxxxxxxx to rt-0f9e8d7c, but that could affect other AZs. I'll re-associate a single subnet as test.

kevin (sre): Hold rollback to a single subset first. Maria, can you coordinate canary and blast radius? We'll re-associate one private subnet (svc-hosts-azc-a) and watch LB errors.

maria (oncall): doing. Re-associating svc-hosts-azc-a to rt-0a1b2c3d now.

oliver (net): command:
```
aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rtbassoc-03abc --route-table-id rt-0a1b2c3d --region us-west-2
```

maria (oncall): Ran replace-route-table-association for rtbassoc-03abc. Watching metrics...

kevin (sre): Metrics updated: 504 rate for that host group drop from 18/min to 2/min in 90s. Good sign.

sophie (support): Customer-facing note: "We’re investigating an issue impacting some requests in the us-west-2 region; mitigation underway. Will update in 15m." :thumbsup:

oliver (net): Re-associating remaining affected private subnets in AZc now in small batches (2 at a time) to avoid route flapping.

maria (oncall): Re-association of all affected subnets in AZc complete. Monitoring for 10min.

kevin (sre): After full rollback, API error rate normalized to baseline. No data plane errors seen. Will keep increased retention on traces for 30 minutes and run postmortem collection.

oliver (net): Root cause hypothesis: infra/PR #432 intended to attach transient route-table for new transit tests but association list included production private subnets for AZc by mistake. Missing 0.0.0.0/0->NAT entry in the transient RT caused egress outage.

maria (oncall): Next steps:
- Rollback association (done) and monitor. (maria, oliver)
- Revert PR #432 and open safety patch to validate route-table content before association. (oliver)
- Postmortem and customer impact summary. (kevin, sophie)
- Add automated lint in CI to ensure route-tables intended for transient use are tagged and associations validated. (infra team)

kevin (sre): Assigning incident severity: Sev 2 (partial outage for subset of hosted customers). Start timeline capture. Paging clear in 28m. Handing to oncall-runbook for postmortem.

sophie (support): Sending customers update: mitigation complete, we’re monitoring metrics closely and will follow up with root cause and timeline.

maria (oncall): Thanks all. tagging followups: #postmortems, #eng-networking. I'll leave this thread open for artifacts. :white_check_mark:
